```{python}
import polars as pl

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)
```


```{python}

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json"
response = requests.get(url)
df = pl.read_json(io.BytesIO(response.content))
```


## QUESTION 1

__Calculate the sample size (i.e. number of rows in the dataset) for each airport in each year__. What do you notice?

_What I noticed is that the sample size varies significantly across airports and years. For example, some airports have a large number of flights in certain years, while others have very few._

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
sample_sizes = (
    df
    .group_by(["airport_name", "year"])
    .count()
    .sort(["airport_name", "year"])
)

sample_sizes

```

## QUESTION 2

__Which airport has the worst delays?__ Describe the metric you chose, and why you chose it to determine the “worst” airport. Your answer should include a summary table that lists (for each airport) the total number of flights, total number of delayed flights, proportion of delayed flights, and average delay time in hours. 

_The metric being used to total delayed flights over total flights. This gives the proportion of flights that are delayed._

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
airport_summary = (
    df
    .group_by(["airport_code", "airport_name"])
    .agg([
        pl.col("num_of_flights_total").sum().alias("total_flights"),
        pl.col("num_of_delays_total").sum().alias("total_delayed_flights"),
        (
            pl.col("num_of_delays_total").sum() /
            pl.col("num_of_flights_total").sum()
        ).alias("proportion_delayed"),
        (
            pl.col("minutes_delayed_total").sum() /
            pl.col("num_of_delays_total").sum() / 60
        ).alias("avg_delay_hours")
    ])
    .sort("proportion_delayed", descending=True)
)

airport_summary

```

## QUESTION 3

__Create a barplot showing the proportion of all flights that are delayed at each airport. Describe what you learn from this graph.__  

_I learned that the airport that has the most delayed flights is ORD airport in Chicago, with almost 30% of its flights being delayed._

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
(
    ggplot(airport_summary)
    + geom_bar(
        aes(
            x="airport_code",
            y="proportion_delayed"
        ),
        stat="identity"
    )
    + labs(
        title="Proportion of Delayed Flights by Airport",
        x="Airport",
        y="Proportion Delayed"
    )
)
```
